findings.description: allocate iterates over the records iterable twice – once to compute total and once to build the result dictionary. This fails for one-shot iterators such as generators, resulting in an empty dictionary.
findings.evidence: When records is a generator, the first sum() exhausts it, so the dictionary comprehension iterates over an empty iterator and returns {} instead of the expected distribution.

review.summary: Candidate implementation incorrectly consumes the records iterable twice, violating the contract that the iterable may be a one-shot iterator and must be consumed only once.
